Ascitic fluid in an HIV-positive male showing dispersed large malignant cells with irregular nuclear contours and coarse chromatin, consistent with primary effusion lymphoma (Giemsa).

Ascitic fluid in an HIV-positive male with single, large atypical lymphoid cells including multinucleated cells with irregular nuclear contours and coarse chromatin, consistent with primary effusion lymphoma (Pap).
Ascitic fluid in an HIV-positive male showing dispersed large malignant cells with irregular nuclear contours and coarse chromatin, consistent with primary effusion lymphoma (Giemsa).

An HHV8-negative 90-year-old man with pleural effusion. Large atypical lymphoid cells vary in size, with highly irregular, pleomorphic, indented, lobated nuclei with coarse chromatin and one or more nucleoli (Giemsa).

HIV-positive patient with pleural effusion. Large single atypical lymphoid cells, with moderately pleomorphic nuclei with coarse granular chromatin, prominent one to three nucleoli, and variable amount of concentric or eccentric cytoplasm, sometimes with a suggestion of a “hof”, that is, perinuclear clearing (Giemsa).
